items.text: The support landing page links to `/docs/support/provider-support-policy/`, which must exist as a page.

Pulumi maintains each provider major version for a defined length of time and provides long-term security updates for a subset of providers (as described by the support-landing-page card for the provider support policy).
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes made during an update when an error or failure occurs.
When an error or failure occurs during a Pulumi update, Pulumi completes any pending operations currently in progress and then exits and reports the error.
Reverting the code and configuration changes of a failed deployment and running `pulumi up` updates the infrastructure back to its previous state (manual rollback).
Pulumi does not automatically query the cloud provider's live state before running `pulumi up` or `pulumi preview`.
Pulumi determines what changes to make by comparing the desired state declared in the program against the last recorded state (the state file), not live cloud state.
A Pulumi refresh requires a round-trip to the cloud provider for every resource in a stack.
Refreshing every resource adds significant latency to Pulumi operations, especially for large stacks.
In Pulumi, changes made outside of Pulumi are treated as drift that the user decides explicitly how to handle.
`pulumi refresh` synchronizes Pulumi's recorded state with the actual state of the cloud resources.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes state and applies the desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for automated drift detection and remediation on a schedule.
The page `/docs/deployments/concepts/drift/` exists.
The page `/docs/iac/concepts/state-and-backends/` exists and has a `#refreshing-state` anchor.
Pulumi resources have distinct logical names and physical names.
A Pulumi resource's logical name is how the resource is known to Pulumi and is part of the auto-assigned resource URN.
A Pulumi resource's physical name is how the resource is known to the cloud provider.
A Pulumi resource's logical name only needs to be unique within a stack.
A resource's physical name typically needs to be unique within a certain cloud-provider scope, sometimes globally.
By default Pulumi auto-names each resource by combining the logical name with a random suffix appended afterwards.
Pulumi auto-naming allows Pulumi to replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement resource before deleting the old one.
An auto-named Pulumi resource's physical name typically looks like `my-bucket-d7c2fa0` (logical name plus a random hex suffix) rather than `my-bucket`.
Pulumi auto-naming can be disabled on a per-resource basis.
The page `/docs/iac/concepts/resources/names/` exists and has an `#autonaming` anchor.
Disabling Pulumi auto-naming for a resource yields a precise physical name but loses the side-by-side uniqueness and create-before-delete replacement benefits.
Pulumi project or stack configuration can customize or disable auto-naming globally, per provider, or per resource type.
The page `/docs/iac/concepts/resources/names/` has an `#autonaming-configuration` anchor.
Pulumi provides primitives to enforce that secrets are stored securely in the CLI, the state file, and Pulumi Cloud.
During a Pulumi update, secrets are decrypted in memory and are visible to the Pulumi program.
The page `/docs/iac/concepts/secrets/` exists and has a `#secrets` anchor.
`pulumi config set` accepts a `--secret` flag that causes the configuration value to be encrypted so it can be safely persisted in `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml`.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key for every stack and uses it to encrypt that stack's secrets.
Pulumi's stack secrets encryption is configurable to use a custom secrets provider instead of the Pulumi Cloud-managed key.
Encrypting the same secret value in two different Pulumi stacks produces different encrypted strings in the respective `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml` files.
An encrypted secret value cannot be copied from one stack's `Pulumi.<stack-name>.yaml` to another's with a text editor; `pulumi config set` must be used instead.
The page `/docs/iac/concepts/config/` exists.
When running a preview, update, or destroy, Pulumi decrypts secret configuration; it is plaintext during execution and accessible to any part of the program via the Pulumi config object.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine in any way.
Some Pulumi providers use open-source Terraform schemas to determine available resources, parameters, and return/response attributes.
Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
The URL `https://www.terraform.io/docs/extend/schemas/index.html` resolves to Terraform schema documentation.
The page `/blog/pulumiup-native-providers/` exists.
Pulumi is a declarative tool that uses imperative programming languages to define the desired end state.
In Pulumi, the programming language is used only for authoring the program and is not used for talking to the cloud provider API.
Pulumi uses strongly typed programming languages that support IntelliSense and the Language Server Protocol.
When defining Pulumi programs you rarely need to leave your IDE.
The URLs `https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/editor/intellisense` and `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Language_Server_Protocol` resolve.
Pulumi experimental features are always opt-in, enabled explicitly via a flag, command, or environment variable.
`PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true` is an environment variable that enables Pulumi experimental functionality.
Pulumi experimental features are not necessarily supported.
Pulumi experimental features can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle.
When an experimental Pulumi feature proves valuable, Pulumi stabilizes it and promotes it to general availability.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (long-term support).
Pulumi's previous-major security updates for covered providers last for up to one year.
Pulumi's previous-major security-update window for a covered provider ends either after one year or when the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page `/docs/support/provider-support-policy/` exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Pulumi provider major versions older than the previous major receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry at `/registry/` shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi recommends that the release of a new provider major version be treated as the signal to begin planning a provider version update.
Pulumi provider major versions typically include significant changes such as deprecations, new resources, and new functionality that may require additional migration steps.
Pulumi recommends updating to the latest minor version on the current provider major at least quarterly and reviewing provider release notes.
Pulumi provider minor versions typically include new resources, features, performance improvements, and bug fixes without breaking changes.
The release notes for each Pulumi provider release summarize the new capabilities or fixes in that release.
In npm, the tilde version operator (e.g. `~1.2.3`) allows patch updates within the current minor version.
Pulumi recommends always allowing patch updates on the current provider minor version.
Pulumi provider patch versions are primarily bug fixes and security updates and are designed to be fully backward compatible.
Pulumi recommends never being two major provider versions behind because jumping a major version is inadvisable given the potential breaking changes.
Each Pulumi provider major version includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version.
Pulumi provider major-version migration logic does not always work across multiple major versions, so being two or more majors behind may require a multi-step upgrade.
The 'Learn more' link `/docs/support/provider-support-policy/` resolves to an existing page.
The pages `/docs/support/faq/secrets-config/`, `/docs/support/faq/pulumi-cloud/`, and `/docs/support/faq/policies/` exist.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (long-term support).
Pulumi's long-term support (N−1) window for a covered provider lasts up to 12 months from the release of the current major N.
Pulumi's long-term support window for a provider's previous major ends at 12 months or when the next major version ships, whichever comes first.
The list of ten providers on the provider support policy page is the current list of providers receiving long-term support updates.
The Pulumi AWS provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Azure Classic provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Azure Native provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Azure AD provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Command provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Docker Build provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi GCP provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi TLS provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.
The Pulumi Vault provider is covered by Pulumi's long-term support policy.

The registry pages `/registry/packages/aws/`, `/registry/packages/azure/`, `/registry/packages/azure-native/`, `/registry/packages/azuread/`, `/registry/packages/command/`, `/registry/packages/docker-build/`, `/registry/packages/gcp/`, `/registry/packages/kubernetes/`, `/registry/packages/tls/`, and `/registry/packages/vault/` each exist.
A Pulumi provider LTS branch ships fixes for High/Critical CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
A Pulumi provider LTS branch ships fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch when needed to ship security patches.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new resources or new resource properties.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain performance improvements.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain non-security bug fixes.
A Pulumi provider LTS release does not add compatibility with newer versions of language runtimes.
Pulumi LTS providers remain compatible with the Pulumi engine version they were frozen at, unless a security fix requires otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered Pulumi provider at any time.
When a covered Pulumi provider ships major N+1, the previous current major N becomes the new LTS major.
When a covered Pulumi provider ships major N+1, the old LTS major (N−1) reaches end of life on the same day, regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within a Pulumi provider's LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are published through the same standard package registries as current-major releases.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are tagged differently from current-major releases in the package registries.
Pulumi recommends pinning to a specific provider major version.
Customers who pin to a specific Pulumi provider major version automatically receive LTS patch releases as they ship.
Pulumi provider major versions at N−2 and older are end of life, are not supported, and receive no patches or updates.
In Pulumi's provider support policy, N denotes the latest released major version: if v3 is newest, v3 is N, v2 is N−1 (LTS), and v1 and earlier are end of life.
A Pulumi provider's current major (N) is supported until N+1 ships.
A Pulumi provider's current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions.
The page `/docs/support/faq/infrastructure/` exists and has a `#what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions` anchor.
The pages `/registry/` and `/docs/support/getting-support/` exist.
